episodic.task: volume render bonsai.raw as a potted tree (brown pot, silver branch, golden leaves)
episodic.what_worked: Measured scalar range at runtime and placed all opacity/color control points as fractions of that range. A hard opacity=0 plateau below ~25% of range removed the low-value speckle haze. Shading on gave the tree 3D form.

params.measured_range_example: [0,255] for this file (reference only, re-measure per dataset)

episodic.outcome: Clear potted bonsai: distinct trunk, branches, bowl pot; haze eliminated.

semantic.rule: Inspect the data's actual scalar min/max at runtime and place every opacity/color control point as a FRACTION of that measured range, never as a fixed scalar value.
Low scalar values are usually background/noise: hold opacity flat at 0 up to a cutoff fraction (~0.2-0.25 of range), then ramp up. This removes the speckle 'haze' that otherwise fogs the render.
Always render then LOOK at the PNG; fix opacity/color before finishing. The first transfer function is rarely right.

corrective.mistake: Gave low-value voxels nonzero opacity, producing a brown speckle 'haze' cloud around the subject.
corrective.fix: Raise the background cutoff: keep opacity 0 until ~0.2-0.25 of the measured range so only real structure is visible.

corrective.mistake: Assumed density increases monotonically with the semantic part (e.g. pot<branch<leaves), which inverted the colors.
corrective.fix: Do not assume which structure is densest. Inspect value distribution (and spatial/height distribution if needed) to decide which scalar band maps to which part before assigning colors.
